before:
Tower Bells Practice Rota — Allocation Settings

The generator fills each Thursday practice from the standing list of eligible ringers. Where more names are entered than there are working bells, the overflow is resolved by a fixed ordering: learners under instruction are seated first, then visiting ringers from associated towers, and only then members who already ring at a second tower. Everyone on the standing list stays eligible for every bell, and nobody is barred from any slot by this setting; the generator simply works down the ordering until the bells are full. Names displaced on one Thursday roll forward to the head of the following week's overflow. The tower captain may not edit a generated sheet except to mark absence.

before:
Sluice Gate Handover — Night Shift Procedure

Night handover at the middle sluice takes place at 22:40. The outgoing keeper reads the gauge board, enters the reading in the shift book, and hands the channel keys to the relief in person; a key left in the hut cupboard does not count as a handover. Where the relief is delayed, the outgoing keeper may go off duty once the shift book has been countersigned by the depot telephonist. The gauge board is read again at 23:10 by whoever holds the keys. Any reading above the amber mark is telephoned to the duty engineer whatever the hour, and the time of the call is entered beside it.
after:
Sluice Gate Handover — Night Shift Procedure

Night handover at the middle sluice takes place at 22:40. before:
Beekeepers' Association — Swarm Collector Register

The register lists members willing to collect swarms inside the parish boundary, with a telephone number and the months each member is free. Entries are refreshed each February from returned slips. When the duty telephone takes a swarm call, the volunteer on the desk reads out the standing reply: 'Someone will come out when one of our lot is free, so keep an eye on it and don't go spraying it.' The caller's address, the height of the swarm and the time of the call are then entered on the day sheet. Members not reached within twenty minutes are passed over and the next name tried. Day sheets are filed with the February slips.

before:
Tide Board Manual — Section 4, Reading the Staff

Section 4. The staff is read from the pontoon walkway at eye level, never from the quay above, and the reading is taken as the mean of crest and trough over ten seconds. Under calm conditions the staff reading is accurate to within twenty millimetres of the true water level. In swell above half a metre the reader records crest and trough separately and marks the entry 'S'. Readings are entered in centimetres to one decimal place. The harbour office compares the day's noon reading against the predicted curve each Friday and flags any entry differing by more than eight centimetres for the master's attention.
after:
Tide Board Manual — Section 4, Reading the Staff

Section 4. The staff is read from the pontoon walkway at eye level, never from the quay above, and the reading is taken as the mean of crest and trough over ten seconds. Under calm conditions the staff reading may be taken as within twenty millimetres of the true water level, though that figure rests on the last resurvey and has not been rechecked since. In swell above half a metre the reader records crest and trough separately and marks the entry 'S'. Readings are entered in centimetres to one decimal place. The harbour office compares the day's noon reading against the predicted curve each Friday and flags any entry differing by more than eight centimetres for the master's attention.
variation_site: The change falls in the sentence about calm-condition reading.
author_note: Hard against empirical: the tolerance figure is left exactly as it was and only the strength of assertion behind it moves.

before:
Reservoir Bulletin — Spring Waterfowl Counts

Bulletin 3. The March count at the lower reservoir was made from the east hide on a still, bright morning with good visibility to the far bank. Counters logged sixty-eight shoveler on the shallows below the outfall, the highest March figure since the hide was rebuilt. Teal were down on last year, eighty-two against a five-year mean of one hundred and ten. Two counters worked the north arm on foot and reported the reed fringe newly cut back by the water company. The next count falls on the second Sunday of April; volunteers should collect a tally card from the warden's box before walking out to their sector.

before:
Village Hall Handbook — Hire Charges

Hire charges are worked out by the booking secretary when the form is returned, not when the event falls. For regular weekly hirers the hourly figure is taken from the county association's recommended scale for halls of comparable seating, with the winter heating supplement added between November and March. Casual hirers pay the same hourly figure plus a single setting-up charge. Deposits are held against breakages and returned within twenty-eight days. Cancellation inside a fortnight forfeits the deposit. The committee reviews the heating supplement each October and posts any change on the porch noticeboard before the winter season opens.

before:
Ferry Slipway Log — Entry Format

The slipway log is kept in the ticket hut and written up at the end of each running day, one line per crossing, in the order the crossings were made. Each line carries the time, then the vehicle count, then foot passengers, then sea state, with the fields separated by a solidus and no spaces, and the date given at the head of the page as day-month-year in figures. Delays of more than ten minutes are noted in the margin with the cause in words. The log is collected on the first of the month by the office launch and a fresh book left in its place. Nothing is erased; corrections are struck through once and initialled.

before:
Angling Club — Membership Classes

Throughout this document a local member means a member whose principal address lies within five miles of the club's water, measured by road from the lodge gate. Local members pay the lower subscription, may vote at the annual meeting, and take precedence on the winter waiting list. Other members pay the full subscription and may fish on any day but Sunday. The secretary checks addresses against the roll each January and moves members between the two classes without further reference to the committee. Members who move house are asked to tell the secretary within a month, since the move may alter what falls due at the next renewal.

before:
Coastal Path Erosion — Annual Report Extract

Extract from the surveyor's annual report on the coastal path between the old lime kiln and the caravan field. The path was walked in October and the previous year's marker pegs were recovered at four of the six stations. At station three the cliff edge has retreated one point four metres since the previous survey, the largest single-year loss yet logged on this stretch. Elsewhere retreat ran between nought point one and nought point four metres. The diversion fence at station three was moved inland in November and the path now runs behind the gorse. Stations five and six could not be re-pegged owing to slumping and will be re-established from the field boundary next spring.
